title.narrative: Global WASH Program(GWP) Phase II, India

description.narrative: In its second phase, the Global WASH Programme (GWP) in India supports systemic transformation in the rural water supply sector, contributing to three key outcomes: Service Delivery Strengthening, Integrated Inclusive Planning, and Accountability and Monitoring.

The India project engages a diverse range of participants across micro, meso, and macro levels, involving both direct and indirect beneficiaries in a system-wide approach to strengthening WASH governance and service delivery.At the micro level, direct beneficiaries include 120 community-based WASH user associations and Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) in the districts of Panna, Newari, and Chhatarpur, as well as approximately 290 local mechanics and operators of piped water systems. In addition, 120 trained community water volunteers (Jal Saheli/Jal Mitra) and 90 WASH forum members benefit from targeted capacity development measures. Indirectly, around 100,000 community members stand to gain from improved water supply, hygiene awareness, and sanitation services.At the meso (district) level, the project supports District Panchayat staff and Public Health Engineering Department (PHED) officials in the three districts, as well as district-level actors from agriculture and irrigation departments. Thirty local CSOs working in these areas are also directly involved. Indirect beneficiaries include all Gram Panchayats within the three districts and an estimated 460,000 residents who will benefit from improved WASH governance and more reliable service delivery.At the macro level, the initiative engages state-level institutions such as PHED, the Jal Jeevan Mission, and Atal Jal Yojna teams, along with 50 CSOs operating across the Bundelkhand region. Indirectly, the entire rural population of Madhya Pradesh may benefit through improved state-level governance, increased investments in sustainable rural water supply under the NRDWM, and broader CSO mobilization through national WASH advocacy networks reaching up to 550 organizations.

This project is part of Phase II of the Global WASH Program (GWP) implemented in SLE, ZWE, PAK and India. Building on Phase I, Phase II of the program focuses on scaling and institutionalizing WASH systems strengthening across five key areas: Service Delivery Strengthening, Inclusive Planning, Accountability & Monitoring, Institutional Arrangements & Coordination, and Learning & Sector Adaptation. A key emphasis is the shift from systems strengthening to systems delivery, ensuring sustainable WASH services for target communities. Phase II embeds these approaches in government structures and policies, reducing dependency on external support. Advocacy and stakeholder collaboration remain vital for financial sustainability and institutional adaptation.
